title: Wall Street slides as Nvidia casts shadow over tech stocks
detail:
Wall Street slides as Nvidia casts shadow over tech stocks
Chris Price
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 11:54 AM CST 26 min read
NVDA
^GSPC
^DJI
^NDX
ANT
Trade NVIDIA on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange - AFP via Getty Images/ANGELA WEISS

Wall Street tech stocks fell sharply on Monday as Nvidia suffered a fresh slide following the Jensen Huang scandal.

The Nasdaq 100 was down 2.1pc in early trading as investors dialled back their bets on the tech sector ahead of a pivotal week for AI stocks.

Nvidia led the fallers, declining by 3.6pc after the US Commerce Department moved to close a loophole that allowed China to rent the chip maker's computing power located in other countries.

The S&P 500 also fell 1.4pc and the Dow Jones was down 0.8pc.

Traders are awaiting a crucial earnings report from Nvidia on Tuesday, followed by Anthropic's potentially record-setting market debut on Thursday.

Nadia El Bilassy, market analyst at Equiti Group, said the success of Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO "will be the barometer for whether the correction will continue or not".

Nvidia's recent decline has heaped pressure on rival AI stocks.

Fellow chipmakers Micron Technology and Advanced Micro Devices were under pressure, down 5.9pc and 4.7pc respectively.

These declines helped pull the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, a grouping of the major chipmakers, down 4pc, its lowest level in a week.

Nvidia shares are down 35pc since their peak after Mr Huang resigned as chief executive last week.

It follows accusations of affairs with two Nvidia employees and another with an alleged Chinese spy.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia, urging its board to look outside the company for its next CEO over the weekend.

However, on Monday, Donald Trump backed calls for Mr Huang to be reinstated as chief executive.

The embattled chipmaker is preparing to report its third-quarter results on Tuesday evening.

Analysts expect the company to post nearly 100pc year-over-year earnings and revenue growth.

Investors will be more focused, however, on how the company will move forward after Mr Huang's exit after 33 years in charge.

Read the latest updates below.

05:54pm

Signing off...

Thank you for following our coverage of the tech sell-off on Wall Street, as investors fret ahead of Nvidia's earnings and Anthropic's IPO on Friday.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was down 2pc on Monday, with Nvidia shares declining 3.6pc ahead of the call.

Donald Trump has said he is open to Jensen Huang, Nvidia's co-founder, returning to the company after resigning following a cheating scandal with an alleged Chinese spy.

Ondas sank 8% even after record revenue and a $1 billion-plus 2027 target, as thin margins and acquisition dilution spook investors; Red Cat slid 5%.

NVIDIA's leadership turmoil and a weaker NASDAQ 100 are hammering high-beta drone names, while AeroVironment's established defense model offers a steadier contrast.

CFO Neil Laird expects gross margins to stay near 35% in Q4, so Ondas must prove its backlog converts into profit.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

Days after the company raised its outlook, investors are putting Ondas (NASDAQ:ONDS) in the show-me category. Ondas stock is trading at $4.77, down 8%. That extends a hard year and leaves the stock down 51% year to date (YTD).

agrusoft / Flickr

Ondas is sliding as investors pull back from growth stocks tied to artificial intelligence (AI). NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA) is falling on reports of a possible leadership change, with its upcoming earnings still ahead. With the NASDAQ 100 down 1.4%, the smaller, high-beta drone names are taking some of the biggest hits.

What Ondas Delivered on November 12

Ondas Holdings posted record Q3 2026 revenue of $167.49 million on November 12. That was up 1,558.6% year over year (YoY) and ahead of the $148.04 million consensus. The company also raised its full-year 2026 revenue target to at least $550 million and set an initial 2027 target of at least $1.1 billion, excluding additional acquisitions. Its backlog reached $835 million. CEO Eric Brock said, "We expect a strong finish to 2026, with momentum accelerating in the fourth quarter as volume deliveries ramp across existing programs."

------

Profitability is where the report disappointed. Ondas Holdings' gross margin contracted to 21.8%. Its loss of $0.10 per share under generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) missed the $0.09 consensus, even with $125.1 million in non-cash warrant gains. Adjusted gross margin was 34.8%. Chief Financial Officer Neil Laird noted on the call. "We expect gross margins to remain in the mid-30% range in the Q4 period due to continued mix of lower-margin revenue."

Acquisitions add a second layer of risk for Ondas. The company deployed $431 million in cash on deals during Q3, and its six acquisitions bring integration risk along with dilution concerns.

ONDS Earnings Explorer — 24/7 Wall St.
Red Cat and Unusual Machines Fall Less Than Ondas

Red Cat Holdings (NASDAQ:RCAT) stock is at $3.60, down 5%. The drop at Red Cat is smaller than the one at Ondas, and it's moving with the broader drone-sector decline.

Unusual Machines (NYSEAMERICAN:UMAC) stock is at $10.84, down 4%. When Unusual Machines reported its Q3 2026 results on November 5, the components maker posted revenue of $13.9 million, up 551.3% YoY. It also posted a narrow loss in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA). Allan Evans, the company's CEO, stated, "I continue to believe that Unusual Machines can achieve positive adjusted EBITDA in 2027 without compromising our growth plans."

AeroVironment (NASDAQ:AVAV) offers a contrast as an established defense contractor. Its established model sets it apart from the high-beta drone stocks.

How Ondas Stacks Up Against Its Drone Peers

Ondas is using acquisitions to build an integrated defense-technology platform that spans counter-unmanned aircraft systems (counter-UAS), precision strike, land systems and independent AI through Regna AI. The portfolio at Ondas also includes Ondas Sentinel, Ondas Autonomous Systems, IonStrike and ULTRA.

Red Cat runs a narrower Family of Systems built around the Black Widow intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) drone, Teal Drones and Blue Ops uncrewed surface vessels. Unusual Machines sits further upstream. It supplies National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)-compliant motors, batteries and cameras through Fat Shark, Rotor Riot and Upgrade Energy. That model ties Unusual Machines to the production volumes of the drone makers it supplies.

AeroVironment is the established prime contractor in the group, with Switchblade loitering munitions, Puma drones and LOCUST directed-energy systems. Its scale and profitability give AeroVironment a buffer that Ondas is still working to build.

Can Ondas Turn Its Backlog Into Profits?

Ondas now has to prove volume deliveries can push Q4 2026 revenue above the $250 million the company guided to. The bulls point to the backlog, the 2027 target and management's decision to pull company-wide adjusted EBITDA profitability forward to Q3 2027 from Q4 2027. Management at Ondas also expects gross margins to reach 45% to 50% over the next 12 to 24 months.

Losses and dilution anchor the bearish case, since Ondas is still losing money while acquisitions add to its share count, and margin recovery at the company hasn't started yet, with management expecting a similar margin profile in Q4.

Ondas has the orders and the targets, and the coming quarters may show whether deliveries can turn them into profits. The debate over Ondas's margin recovery could keep the stock volatile until it settles.

The selloff in Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) is hitting Strategy (NASDAQ:MSTR) hard. Strategy stock is at $102.50, down 8% in morning trading. Measured year to date (YTD), the stock is down 33%.

Bitcoin is at $64,334, down 2% over the past 24 hours and down 17% since the end of October. Strategy disclosed on November 16 that it bought 485 Bitcoin between November 9 and November 15 for $33.4 million, funded by sales of its common stock. The purchase lifts Strategy's holdings to 850,849 BTC at a reported average cost of $75,452 per coin, a level above where Bitcoin trades now.

Buybacks took a far bigger slice of the week's spending, with Strategy putting $228.1 million into repurchases of its STRC preferred stock. That mix signals a slower pace of Bitcoin accumulation for the company, while the common stock sales behind the purchase raise dilution concerns.

Index selling adds a second overhang for Strategy. On November 11, the provider of the MSCI USA Index said it'd drop the company after the close on November 30, so funds tracking that benchmark must sell their shares by then. The exit extends across the provider's global indexes as well, expanding the pool of passive sellers.

Retail view on Strategy is split. One camp calls the drop a buying opportunity. Another warns of more downside tied to paper losses on the treasury, dilution and index-related selling.

Coinbase and MARA Fall Less Than Strategy

Coinbase Global (NASDAQ:COIN) stock is at $118.40, down 7%. That decline is smaller than Strategy's, consistent with an exchange whose revenue tracks trading activity and stablecoin balances. During Q3 2026, Coinbase's revenue fell 35% year over year (YoY) as crypto volatility hit multi-year lows, so a selloff doesn't automatically bring a trading windfall.

MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA) stock is at $6.53, down 7%. A 37% decline in the average price of Bitcoin mined cut MARA's Q3 revenue by $94.8 million, even as the company's hashrate grew. Riot Platforms (NASDAQ:RIOT) is another exposed miner.

How Strategy's Model Differs From Coinbase and the Miners

Strategy pairs an enterprise analytics software business with the largest corporate Bitcoin treasury, financed through common stock sales, convertible notes and several series of preferred stock. This structure amplifies Bitcoin's moves in both directions, and the company owes preferred dividends wherever the coin trades, with quarterly profits at Strategy rising and falling alongside the coin's value because the software revenue is small next to Bitcoin swings.

Coinbase runs a regulated exchange that makes transaction fees plus subscription and services revenue, led by stablecoin income. MARA and Riot mine Bitcoin, so their output loses value when the coin drops, yet both are building AI data center businesses around their power assets. Riot has signed long-term leases with a major chipmaker. It has also signed leases with a frontier AI lab, while MARA is adding a natural gas plant and a private AI cloud business.

Strategy's Cost-Basis Squeeze Meets an Index Deadline

Strategy's next test is whether Bitcoin climbs back above the company's average cost before index funds finish selling on November 30. Executive Chairman Michael Saylor stated on October 29 that Bitcoin is "at the beginning of its next bull market," and a rebound could restore the treasury's cushion.

The index exit looks like a one-time overhang to bulls, with Strategy's full Bitcoin exposure intact for any recovery. Slower buying, ongoing dilution and the preferred dividend load are what the bears cite, and each could weigh further on Strategy if the coin keeps decline.

Each scenario runs through Bitcoin, which ties Strategy's next move to the coin's direction. Investors may want to track how Strategy's MSCI index exit resolves.

title: Demand for the Anthropic IPO Far Outpaces Available Shares. Be Careful in an Early Scramble for Stock.

Buying shares in Anthropic (ANT) could soon become an option for everyday investors as its upcoming initial public offering (IPO) draws Wall Street's attention. The Nasdaq 100 ($IUXX) jumped on Nov. 11 as encouraging artificial intelligence (AI) earnings and strong demand for Anthropic's upcoming IPO helped lift market sentiment.

Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, is preparing to list under the ticker "ANT," giving public market investors a chance to own a stake in the business. But the opportunity to buy and the ability to secure shares on attractive terms are two different things.

More News from Barchart

Why It's Time to Load Up on CoreWeave Stock

Dear AST SpaceMobile Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 17

How to Play Alibaba Stock Ahead of Its T-Head Spinoff and IPO

Our exclusive Barchart Brief newsletter is your FREE midday guide to what's moving stocks, sectors, and investor sentiment - delivered right when you need the info most. Subscribe today!

With so many investors eager to get in, what could the competition for shares mean for the allocation you receive and the price you ultimately pay? Let's find out.

What Oversubscription Means for Retail Buyers

Anthropic's IPO has attracted orders for multiple times the available shares, meaning investors have requested more stock than the offering can accommodate. Bankers have reportedly told prospective buyers that existing backers will receive priority, potentially leaving newcomers with smaller allocations than they hoped to secure ahead of the company's public debut.

Individual investors nevertheless have a designated opening. Anthropic plans to allocate up to 20% of its offering's 825 million shares to retail buyers. That represents as many as 165 million shares, worth approximately $12.2 billion at the proposed $74 midpoint per-share price. However, the final retail allocation remains subject to demand, so those figures represent a potential maximum rather than a guaranteed pool of shares available to individual applicants.

Even within that pool, buyers could receive fewer shares than requested or miss out altogether. Overall oversubscription does not reveal an applicant's allocation odds, and the reported preference for existing backers does not establish how the separate retail allocation will be distributed.

Buyers who miss out may consider purchasing once trading begins, but an early premium could later fade. Retail investors, therefore, face uncertainty over both access and price. They may secure a smaller initial stake than planned, then pay more to complete their position, increasing their average purchase cost and the risk of losses if early enthusiasm gives way to selling.

What Anthropic Is Bringing to Market

Anthropic expects to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Nov. 19. The offering comprises 801.4 million new Class A shares and 23.6 million shares from existing holders, whose proceeds will not go to the company. Underwriters have a 30-day option to purchase another 123.75 million shares.

The proposed $70 to $78 price range implies a valuation of approximately $1.3 trillion at the midpoint and $1.4 trillion at the upper end. At the highest proposed price, the public offering could generate approximately $64.4 billion in gross proceeds. Combined with a separate $26 billion Class N private placement, gross transaction proceeds could reach $90.4 billion. Final pricing remains pending.

Behind those figures is a rapidly expanding business with substantial spending obligations. Anthropic's revenue reached $33.2 billion in the first nine months of 2026, compared with $2.5 billion in the same period of 2025.

Supporting that growth requires substantial investment, with computing and infrastructure commitments totaling $895.4 billion through 2045, including $447.5 billion expected by the end of 2030. The company's reported $3.4 billion deal covering 1.7 gigawatts of generator capacity further illustrates the power requirements behind that expansion.

Despite this growth, valuation expectations have shifted ahead of the listing. On Hyperliquid, a derivative tracking Anthropic's implied valuation fell nearly 30% from its September peak. That movement reflects speculative contract pricing rather than a decline in publicly traded Anthropic shares.

Alongside its commercial expansion, Anthropic has committed 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund. Together with other philanthropic pledges, approximately 20% of company shares are dedicated to "public good" initiatives, extending its public benefit mission into its financial commitments.

What Analysts Make of Investor Appetite

The rush for Anthropic shares has reportedly led Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley to consider pricing the offering above the proposed $78 ceiling. That suggests the banks leading the deal see room to ask buyers for more, although their confidence in selling the shares differs from an independent assessment of their value.

That distinction becomes clearer when looking at the skeptics. Research firm New Constructs called the offering the "most ridiculous IPO of 2026," questioning whether customer spending can support Anthropic's substantial computing obligations. The concern is that the company has committed to infrastructure costs without securing equally durable customer revenue commitments.

Michael Burry shares that concern. He warned that Anthropic is "betting its entire existence on that optimism," pointing to contracts that require payment for computing capacity even when it isn't needed. Those obligations could squeeze margins if demand disappoints. Burry said he had no plans to pursue shares.

Jim Osman, founder of The Edge Group and a specialist in spinoffs and other corporate restructuring opportunities, leaves more room for the business to prove itself. He recognizes Anthropic's growth but wants clearer evidence of sustainable margins and what shareholders retain after infrastructure suppliers are paid.

Conclusion

Anthropic's crowded IPO means retail buyers could receive fewer shares than requested or pay more once trading begins. The likeliest outcome is an early scramble for shares, followed by closer scrutiny of whether earnings prospects justify the price. That leaves buyers balancing limited access against the risk of overpaying. Missing an allocation could feel frustrating, but chasing a jump would add another risk. The better outcome is owning shares at a price that makes sense, even if that means waiting.
